item.title: Measures in Nairian models, I
item.description: arXiv:2610.19088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming $\mathrm{AD}^+ + V = L(P(\mathbb{R}))$, we show that the Ultrapower Axiom holds in $\mathrm{HOD}_s$ for every $\omega$-sequence of ordinals $s$. We use this result to analyze the structure of Nairian models, showing that they contain many measurable cardinals. As an application, we establish the consistency of the existence of infinitely many consecutive measurable cardinals with ZF, starting with a Woodin limit of Woodin cardinals. This solves a question of Henle, Mathias, and Woodin. From the same large cardinal hypothesis, adapting a forcing technique of Adkisson and Ben-Neria, we produce a model of ZF in which every uncountable cardinal is singular. Gitik's original construction requires a proper class of strongly compact cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Goldberg, Grigor Sargsyan

item.title: What David Teaches Goliath: An Inevitable Extension of ZFC
item.description: arXiv:2610.19283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the metamathematical significance of the Levy scheme $\Lambda$, which asserts, for each natural number $n$, the existence of an $n$-Mahlo cardinal $\kappa$ such that $V_\kappa\prec_{\Sigma_n}V$. Several initially unrelated constructions single out $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$: comparisons with the model theory of arithmetic and finite set theory; class theories in which the class of ordinals has the tree property; set theories with a proper class of indiscernibles; and interpretations of ordinary set theory in Cantorian parts of models of the extension $\mathsf{NFUA}$ of Quine--Jensen set theory $\mathsf{NFU}$. Taken together, these results provide a precise sense in which $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ is an inevitable extension of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ if one attempts to generalize certain metamathematical results about the universe of all finite sets to the entire universe of sets.
item.dc:creator: Ali Enayat

item.title: A Reflection Calculus for Bar Induction and the Linearity of Consistency Strength Ordering
item.description: arXiv:2610.20115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a novel extension of reflection calculus, $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$, to analyze a family of extensions of $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ generated by uniform $\omega$-model and syntactic reflection principles, together with several other related operators. The union of these theories coincides with the theory of Bar Induction ($\mathsf{BI}$). We prove that $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$ is arithmetically sound, and that it is sound and complete with respect to a natural class of Kripke models. Leveraging these modal semantics, we demonstrate that the class of theories denoted by $\nabla$-free closed formulas is a pre-wellordering with respect to $\Pi^1_1$-soundness and consistency strength. This allows us to establish an ordinal analysis for $\mathsf{BI}$ and its fragments, analogous to Beklemishev's analysis of $\mathsf{PA}$. The structural properties of $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$ naturally give rise to a novel ordinal notation system for the Bachmann-Howard ordinal which differs substantially from existing representations.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Pakhomov, Vlad Lazar

item.title: The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.19689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$. Finally, we establish $\mathrm{RIGP}$ over the variety-excluding fields of Szachniewicz and the author, when the excluded variety is a locally closed subvariety of an abelian variety.
item.dc:creator: Jinhe Ye

item.title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $\omega$-Categorical Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.19940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct countable, stable, $\omega$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $\omega$-categorical graphs $M_\alpha$ for suitable irrational parameters $\alpha>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_\alpha$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $\alpha$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_\alpha$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Bodirsky, David Bradley-Williams, Ehud Hrushovski, Christoph Spiess

item.title: Convex Team Logics
item.description: arXiv:2503.21850v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove expressive completeness results for convex propositional and modal team logics, where a logic is convex if, for each formula, if it is true in two teams $t$ and $u$ and $t\subseteq s\subseteq u$, then it is also true in $s$. We introduce propositional/modal team logics which are expressively complete for the class of all convex propositional/modal team properties. We also answer an open question concerning the expressive power of classical propositional logic extended with the nonemptiness atom NE: we show that it is expressively complete for the class of all convex and union-closed properties. A modal analogue of this result additionally yields an expressive completeness theorem for Aloni's (2022) Bilateral State-Based Modal Logic. There is a specific sense in which one of the propositional convex logics we introduce extends propositional dependence logic; this sense corresponds to the existence of a compositional translation between the two logics. Another of the convex logics extends propositional inquisitive logic in the same manner. We generalize the notion of uniform definability, as considered in the team semantics literature, to formalize this notion of compositional extension.
item.dc:creator: Aleksi Anttila, S{\o}ren Brinck Knudstorp

item.title: A Note on a Theorem of Apter
item.description: arXiv:2603.08915v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF} + \mathrm{AD}_{\mathbb{R}} + ``\Theta$ is measurable$"$ implies the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF} +``\Theta$ is the least strongly regular cardinal and the least measurable cardinal$"$ + $``$all uncountable cardinals below $\Theta$ are of countable cofinality$"$.
item.dc:creator: Rahman Mohammadpour, Otto Rajala, Sebastiano Thei

item.title: Hindman and Owings-like theorems without the Axiom of Choice
item.description: arXiv:2603.27163v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Hindman- and Owings-type Ramsey-theoretic statements in Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory without the Axiom of Choice, with some occasional extra assumptions (such as the Axiom of Dependent Choice and/or the Axiom of Determinacy). We study several variations of Hindman's theorem on $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; notably, we show that the uncountable analog of Hindman's theorem fails for the additive group of $\mathbb R$ (under ZF), and for $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces of uncountable dimension (under DC if such dimension is not well-orderable), among other results. In contrast, for Owings-type configurations, we obtain several positive results, especially when assuming AD. These results highlight the interaction between determinacy, algebraic structure, and dimension in the study of infinite Ramsey theory without the Axiom of Choice.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e A. Guzm\'an-Vega, David J. Fern\'andez Bret\'on, Eliseo Sarmiento Rosales

item.title: Constructive equivalence between Brouwer's fixed-point theorem and weak K\"onig's lemma
item.description: arXiv:2609.04644v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the context of constructive reverse mathematics, we show that Brouwer's fixed-point theorem and weak K\"onig's lemma (WKL) are equivalent. To derive WKL from Brouwer's fixed-point theorem, the construction of a continuous function on the unit square without fixed points due to Orevkov [Soviet Math. Doklady (1963), 1253--1256] is generalised to yield a uniformly continuous function on the unit square whose fixed points encode information about infinite paths of a given infinite tree.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuji Kawai

item.title: Bluebirds and mockingbirds cannot produce a fixed-point combinator
item.description: arXiv:2609.21765v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $B$ be the bluebird combinator with reduction rule $Bxyz \to_{w} x\left(yz\right)$, let $M$ be the mockingbird combinator with reduction rule $Mx \to_{w} xx$, and let $I$ be the identity bird combinator with reduction rule $Ix \to_{w} x$. A fixed-point combinator, called a sage bird by Smullyan, is a closed term $Y$ such that, for a fresh variable $x$, $Yx$ is equivalent to $x\left(Yx\right)$ under these reduction rules. For a fixed variable $x$, we construct an invariant $\mathrm{Tr}_{x}\left(u\right)$ of a $BMI$-term $u$ with respect to $\to_{w}$. This invariant traces the occurrences of $x$ in the leftmost-innermost reduction sequence of $u$. We then prove that $\mathrm{Tr}_{x}\left(Yx\right) \neq \mathrm{Tr}_{x}\left(x^{r}\left( Yx \right)\right)$ for every $x$-free $BMI$-term $Y$ and every $r\geq 1$. Consequently, there exists no fixed-point combinator in $BMI$-combinatory logic. This provides a negative answer to the problem posed by Smullyan in 1985.
item.dc:creator: Takuma Imamura

item.title: Solution to Dixmier's Problem about spectra of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.26319v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dixmier asked in 1967 whether the spectra of simple separable non-type-I $C^*$-algebras all have the same Borel structure. We solve the formulation using ordinary isomorphisms of quotient Borel $\sigma$-algebras by proving that its universal assertion is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC. Under the continuum hypothesis, all separable non-type-I spectra are measurably isomorphic, without simplicity or unitality assumptions. In the model obtained by iterating Sacks forcing for $\omega_2$ stages with countable supports over a GCH ground model, a fixed simple unital universal spectrum is not measurably isomorphic to the CAR spectrum. Neither consistency direction requires a large cardinal. The Borel-definable formulation, which requires isomorphisms to admit Borel lifts between irreducible representations, has a negative answer in ZFC. For the CAR algebra $A$ and a simple separable exact crossed product $B$ associated to $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$, there is no Borel-definable injection $\widehat B\to\widehat A$. Nevertheless, all separable nuclear non-type-I spectra are Borel-definably isomorphic. We also determine the answer under several choiceless hypotheses. The axiom of determinacy together with dependent choice gives a stronger negative conclusion: the spectrum of $B$ does not even inject as a set into the spectrum of $A$. The symmetric Solovay model gives the same conclusion. Over ZF, a wellordering of the reals of order type $\omega_1$ suffices for a positive answer. The finite-permutation Feferman--Levy model gives another positive answer for the full sigma-generated Borel structures. These comparisons concern the quotient structures themselves, without measure completion.
item.dc:creator: Martino Lupini
